issues.summary: Quiet hours validation may accept invalid edge cases (e.g., quietStart == quietEnd).
issues.evidence: Diff shows inQuietHours function with wraparound logic (`p.quietStart <= p.quietEnd ? ... : ...`) and API validation that checks only 0–23 bounds (TRIAGE spot-check, unconfirmed). If quietStart == quietEnd, the quiet-hours range is empty and will never trigger.
issues.scenario: User sets quietStart=10, quietEnd=10 via API (both pass validation). inQuietHours will return false for all hours, so quiet hours never activate.
issues.fix: Add validation: reject requests where quietStart == quietEnd or (if both set and non-wrapping) quietStart >= quietEnd.
issues.confirm_or_refute: Full code review of API validation, inQuietHours logic, and integration tests for quiet-hours edge cases.
issues.next_action: Reviewer or Author: confirm or refute via full read of notificationPrefs.ts and unit tests for quiet-hours logic.

issues.summary: Database migration backfill uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; semantics unclear and may mask issues.
issues.evidence: Migration SQL: `INSERT INTO notification_prefs (user_id) SELECT id FROM users ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;` (TRIAGE spot-check). This is defensive but unusual; the condition is not obvious from diff alone. No comment explains the expected data state or when conflicts could occur.
issues.scenario: If a previous run partially completed the backfill, re-running the migration will silently skip those rows instead of erroring. Deployments that execute migrations multiple times could silently leave gaps.
issues.fix: Clarify: either add a comment explaining the conflict scenario, or remove ON CONFLICT and rely on the migration tool to retry/fail. If intentional for safety, document the design.
issues.confirm_or_refute: Author clarifies deployment model: are migrations idempotent by design? Full review of migration safety during staged deploy.
issues.next_action: Author: clarify migration design. Reviewer: confirm idempotency semantics match deploy process.
